portableValidation.executionContentComparison: Exact match for every execution row, fixture, cache/work state, control and hook count in both portable replays.

portableValidation.status: Exact original-content match for every execution row, fixture, cache/work state and hook count.

privateStateExtension.role: Supplied movement-service object with invalid handle

fixtureInputs.suppliedCapFormula: float32(weaponSpeed * stanceLabelMultiplier * tagLabel), with one final rounding
initialLevels: One float32 ULP below supplied cap

numericFindings.capOvershootInterpretation: Final post-helper endpoints can exceed the supplied cap by one float32 ULP. These cases do not prove any particular upstream cap construction.

historicalTestRegressions.scope: One native step from each supplied historical-test state; no claim that the native game produced the prior stance ramp.

limits: All stance flags, weapon getter speeds, processed caps and schedules are explicitly supplied.
The upstream native stance/tag/cap-modifier pipeline is not invoked or newly validated.
Same finite grounded arithmetic as the combined replay, with only existing walk/crouch branches enabled.
Walking uses an explicitly invalid movement-service handle; other handle cases remain outside this replay.
Tag factors label supplied caps only; tag recovery/application is outside this replay.
No new native code, accessor hook, collision, physical input replay or complete command dispatcher.
MXCSR profiles, zero external owner velocity, unit owner/surface factors and unscoped dry state are supplied.
Explicit supplied states and schedules, not live physical input replay.
Standing, unscoped, dry ground only; ordinary getter results and scaling/debug settings are supplied private inputs.
Weapon labels map supplied cap values; this harness does not invoke the real per-weapon getter implementations.
Native finite nonzero wish normalization is invoked; min(length,supplied cap) is the retained MINSS selection reproduced by the harness.
Native acceleration, overshoot budget, final cap/work correction, pre/stop/post and wish copy execute; collision and position publishing do not.
Temporary preparation, marker lifecycle and saved-fraction boundaries remain byte-bound harness operations.
Derived uncollided displacement is authored; no complete WalkMove or complete command dispatcher is invoked.
MXCSR is explicitly supplied, not sampled from a live process.
Explicit supplied initial state, processed wish and command schedules; no live physical input replay.
Native selected blocks only: no Accelerate, collision, complete WalkMove, pawn publishing or full command dispatcher.
The stop predicate is executed after the pre helper and before the post helper; non-taken collision path is omitted.
Nonzero-wish controls test cache/friction/stop state without acceleration.
Zero owner external vector and unit owner/surface factors are supplied.
Active saved-fraction insertion, temporary preparation and command-marker lifecycle are byte-bound harness rules.
Derived position is zero when the native stop branch skips position movement; otherwise supplied uncollided midpoint integration.
Thresholds use supplied speeds and float32(.34); GetInaccuracy is not invoked.
MXCSR settings are explicit supplied profiles, not observed runtime configuration.

staticRules: Current class schema binds active stash, saved fraction, stashed speed and previous wish.
The completed segment copies current processed wish XY into previous wish before the next input edge.
An active saved interior fraction is included in later command segmentation; command marker reset/handoff remains a supplied harness rule.
Processed forward/side/up are multiplied separately by the processed cap; wish is stored before direction normalization.
Friction produces velocity, acceleration work and overshoot; acceleration subtracts overshoot divided by duration from its budget.
The native final cap adds its velocity correction to acceleration work before midpoint preparation.
The post-midpoint native stop gate uses the full float32 projected XYZ norm and clears motion only below one.
scope: Supplied unscoped dry-ground numeric replays. The combined replay is standing only; the separate stance replay enables existing walk/crouch branches with supplied processed caps. Upstream stance/tag modifiers and scoped behavior remain outside these replays.
notEstablished: Full native command or physical input latency replay
Collision/terrain or live position publishing parity
Existing-instance reset ownership across every movement mode
